<style>
  :root{
    --bg:#0f1218; --panel:#161b24; --panel2:#1c2230;
    --ink:#e8ecf1; --mute:#9aa4b2; --line:#2a3242;
    --yellow:#ffd866; --blue:#58c4dd; --green:#83c167;
    --pink:#e07a5f; --violet:#b39ddb; --cyan:#7de0d6;
  }
  *{box-sizing:border-box}
  html,body{margin:0;padding:0;background:var(--bg);color:var(--ink);
    font-family:-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,"Segoe UI",Inter,Roboto,sans-serif;
    font-size:17px;line-height:1.65}
  a{color:var(--blue)}
  code{font-family:ui-monospace,SFMono-Regular,Menlo,Consolas,monospace;
    background:#0b0f16;padding:1px 6px;border-radius:4px;color:#f0c987;font-size:0.92em}
  main{max-width:880px;margin:0 auto;padding:4rem 1.5rem 8rem}
  h1{font-size:2.4rem;letter-spacing:-0.01em;margin:0 0 0.4rem}
  h2{font-size:1.6rem;margin:3.2rem 0 0.8rem;color:#fff;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);padding-bottom:.4rem}
  h3{font-size:1.15rem;margin:1.8rem 0 .6rem;color:var(--yellow)}
  p{margin:0.7rem 0}
  .sub{color:var(--mute);margin-top:0;margin-bottom:2rem}
  .widget{background:var(--panel);border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:10px;
    padding:1rem 1.1rem 1.2rem;margin:1.2rem 0}
  .widget .hd{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:baseline;margin-bottom:.6rem;gap:.8rem;flex-wrap:wrap}
  .widget .hd .ttl{font-weight:600;color:#fff;font-size:.95rem;letter-spacing:.02em;text-transform:uppercase}
  .widget .hd .hint{color:var(--mute);font-size:.85rem}
  .row{display:flex;gap:.6rem;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;margin:.4rem 0}
  .row label{color:var(--mute);font-size:.88rem}
  input[type="text"],input[type="number"],select{
    background:#0b0f16;color:var(--ink);border:1px solid var(--line);
    border-radius:6px;padding:.35rem .55rem;font-family:inherit;font-size:.95rem}
  input[type="range"]{accent-color:var(--yellow);flex:1;max-width:260px}
  button{background:var(--panel2);color:var(--ink);border:1px solid var(--line);
    border-radius:6px;padding:.35rem .7rem;cursor:pointer;font:inherit}
  button:hover{background:#242c3e}
  button.active{background:var(--yellow);color:#111;border-color:var(--yellow)}
  .readout{background:#0b0f16;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:6px;
    padding:.6rem .8rem;font-family:ui-monospace,monospace;font-size:.92rem;color:#cbd5e1;
    min-height:1.6em;white-space:pre-wrap;word-break:break-word}
  .pill{display:inline-block;background:var(--panel2);border:1px solid var(--line);
    border-radius:999px;padding:1px 8px;font-size:.82rem;color:var(--mute);margin-right:4px}
  .note{border-left:3px solid var(--violet);padding:.3rem .9rem;color:#d8d2ef;background:#1a1828;
    margin:1rem 0;border-radius:0 6px 6px 0}
  .ok{border-left:3px solid var(--green);padding:.3rem .9rem;color:#d5ebc8;background:#1a2418;
    margin:1rem 0;border-radius:0 6px 6px 0}
  .bad{border-left:3px solid var(--pink);padding:.3rem .9rem;color:#f4d2c7;background:#2a1a18;
    margin:1rem 0;border-radius:0 6px 6px 0}
  svg{display:block;margin:0 auto;max-width:100%}
  svg text{fill:var(--ink);font-family:inherit}
  nav.toc{position:sticky;top:0;background:rgba(15,18,24,.93);backdrop-filter:blur(8px);
    border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);padding:.6rem 1rem;z-index:10;
    display:flex;gap:1rem;flex-wrap:wrap;font-size:.9rem}
  nav.toc a{color:var(--mute);text-decoration:none}
  nav.toc a:hover{color:var(--yellow)}
  /* sticky sidebar TOC (wide screens only; narrow screens fall back to top-nav) */
  aside.sidetoc{position:fixed;top:4.2rem;
    left:max(1rem, calc(50% - 440px - 220px));
    width:200px;max-height:calc(100vh - 6rem);overflow-y:auto;
    padding-right:1rem;border-right:1px solid var(--line);
    font-size:.88rem;z-index:5}
  aside.sidetoc .sidetoc-title{font-size:.7rem;letter-spacing:.14em;text-transform:uppercase;
    color:var(--mute);margin:0 0 .5rem;padding-bottom:.35rem;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line)}
  aside.sidetoc ol{list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0}
  aside.sidetoc li{margin:0}
  aside.sidetoc a{display:block;padding:.3rem .5rem;color:var(--mute);text-decoration:none;
    border-left:2px solid transparent;line-height:1.35;
    transition:color 120ms ease, border-color 120ms ease}
  aside.sidetoc a:hover{color:var(--ink)}
  aside.sidetoc a.active{color:var(--yellow);border-left-color:var(--yellow)}
  @media (max-width:1180px){ aside.sidetoc{display:none} }
  @media (min-width:1181px){ nav.toc a[href^="#"]{display:none} }
  .hero{padding:3rem 0 1rem}
  .small{font-size:.88rem;color:var(--mute)}
  footer{color:var(--mute);font-size:.88rem;text-align:center;margin-top:4rem}
  table.plain{width:100%;border-collapse:collapse;font-size:.95rem;margin:.6rem 0}
  table.plain th,table.plain td{padding:.35rem .5rem;border-bottom:1px solid var(--line);text-align:left}
  table.plain th{color:var(--mute);font-weight:500}
  /* callback-css-auto-begin */
  aside.callback{
    margin:1.2rem 0;padding:.7rem 1rem;
    background:rgba(88,196,221,0.05);
    border-left:3px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--cyan) 45%, transparent);
    border-radius:0 6px 6px 0;
    font-size:.93rem;
  }
  aside.callback .ttl{
    font-size:.68rem;letter-spacing:.14em;text-transform:uppercase;
    color:var(--mute,#8c9aa6);margin-bottom:.3rem;font-weight:600;
  }
  aside.callback ul{margin:0;padding-left:1.1rem}
  aside.callback ul li{margin:.15rem 0}
  aside.callback a{color:inherit}
/* callback-css-auto-end */
  details.changelog{
    margin:2rem 0 1rem;padding:.6rem .9rem;
    background:rgba(0,0,0,0.22);
    border-radius:6px;
    font-size:.85rem;
  }
  details.changelog summary{
    cursor:pointer;letter-spacing:.1em;text-transform:uppercase;
    font-size:.7rem;color:var(--mute,#8c9aa6);
  }
  details.changelog table{margin-top:.5rem;border-collapse:collapse;width:100%;font-size:.82rem}
  details.changelog td{padding:.2rem .6rem;border-bottom:1px dashed rgba(255,255,255,0.07);vertical-align:top}
  details.changelog td:first-child{color:var(--mute,#8c9aa6);white-space:nowrap;font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums}
  aside.related{
    margin:1.2rem 0;padding:.7rem 1rem;
    background:color-mix(in srgb, var(--mute) 6%, transparent);
    border-left:3px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--mute) 55%, transparent);
    border-radius:0 6px 6px 0;
    font-size:.93rem;
  }
  aside.related .ttl{
    font-size:.68rem;letter-spacing:.14em;text-transform:uppercase;
    color:var(--mute,#8c9aa6);margin-bottom:.3rem;font-weight:600;
  }
  aside.related > div{margin:.15rem 0}
  aside.related .more{color:var(--mute);font-style:italic}
  aside.related a{color:inherit}
  /* display-prefs-css-auto-begin */
  html[data-hide-widgets] .widget { display: none !important; }
  html[data-hide-quizzes] .quiz { display: none !important; }
  html[data-hide-lineage] .lineage-strip { display: none !important; }
  .mv-display-toggles { display: inline-flex; gap: .6rem; align-items: center; }
  .mv-display-toggle { background: transparent; border: 1px solid var(--line, #333); border-radius: 6px; padding: 5px 10px; cursor: pointer; font-size: 1.05rem; line-height: 1; color: inherit; transition: background 120ms ease, border-color 120ms ease; }
  .mv-display-toggle:hover { background: var(--panel, rgba(255,255,255,0.06)); border-color: var(--mute, #666); }
  .mv-display-toggle--off { opacity: 0.35; }
  /* display-prefs-css-auto-end */

Topological data analysis

Hand a computer a finite point cloud and ask what shape is this? TDA's answer: thicken every point into a ball of radius $\epsilon$, build the resulting simplicial complex, read off its homology, and watch how features are born and die as $\epsilon$ grows. The persistence diagram is stable, computable in polynomial time, and the basis of an entire applied-topology toolkit.

blocks.html:
1. Point clouds & filtrations

The starting datum is a finite set $X = \{x_1, \dots, x_n\} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$. We want to assign a shape to $X$ — a topological invariant that does not depend on a particular triangulation or smoothing. The move is to thicken: replace each point by a closed ball $B(x_i, \epsilon)$, study the union $X_\epsilon = \bigcup_i B(x_i,\epsilon)$, and let the radius $\epsilon$ vary.

By the nerve theorem, the homotopy type of $X_\epsilon$ is captured by an abstract simplicial complex. The Čech complex $\check C_\epsilon(X)$ has a $k$-simplex $\sigma = \{x_{i_0},\dots,x_{i_k}\}$ whenever $\bigcap_j B(x_{i_j},\epsilon) \neq \emptyset$. The Vietoris–Rips complex is the easier-to-compute cousin:

$\mathrm{VR}_\epsilon(X) \;=\; \{\sigma \subset X : \mathrm{diam}(\sigma) \le 2\epsilon\}.$

Rips uses pairwise distances only — no intersections of multiple balls — so it can be built from a distance matrix alone. The interleaving $\check C_\epsilon \subseteq \mathrm{VR}_\epsilon \subseteq \check C_{\sqrt{2}\,\epsilon}$ means the two have indistinguishable persistent homology up to a scale factor, which is why VR is the default in software.

As $\epsilon$ grows from $0$ to $\infty$, complexes nest:

$\mathrm{VR}_{\epsilon_0}(X) \subseteq \mathrm{VR}_{\epsilon_1}(X) \subseteq \cdots \subseteq \mathrm{VR}_{\epsilon_n}(X) = \Delta^{n-1}.$

This nested family is a filtration. At $\epsilon=0$ it is $n$ isolated points; at $\epsilon=\infty$ it is the full simplex on $X$, which is contractible. Everything interesting happens between.

Points are drawn at radius $\epsilon$. A pair of points is joined by an edge iff their distance is $\le 2\epsilon$; a triple becomes a filled triangle iff all three pairwise distances are $\le 2\epsilon$. The readout reports the number of vertices, edges, and triangles, plus the (rank-0, rank-1) Betti numbers $\beta_0, \beta_1$ computed by reduction. The "annulus" preset reveals a single loop ($\beta_1 = 1$) over a clear window of $\epsilon$.

<script>
(function(){
  const sl=$('#tda-eps'), ev=$('#tda-eps-v'), svg=$('#tda-rips-svg'), out=$('#tda-rips-out'), btn=$('#tda-pattern');
  let dataset = 0;
  const datasets = ['annulus','two-circle','random'];
  function tdaSeed(seed){
    let s = seed|0;
    return function(){
      s = (s + 0x6D2B79F5)|0;
      let t = Math.imul(s ^ s>>>15, s | 1);
      t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ t>>>7, t | 61);
      return ((t ^ t>>>14) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
    };
  }
  function buildPoints(kind){
    const rng = tdaSeed(0xC0FFEE);
    const pts=[];
    if(kind==='annulus'){
      for(let i=0;i<22;i++){
        const a = 2*Math.PI*i/22 + 0.07*(rng()-0.5);
        const r = 1 + 0.08*(rng()-0.5);
        pts.push([r*Math.cos(a), r*Math.sin(a)]);
      }
    } else if(kind==='two-circle'){
      for(let i=0;i<14;i++){
        const a = 2*Math.PI*i/14 + 0.05*(rng()-0.5);
        pts.push([-1.1 + 0.6*Math.cos(a), 0.6*Math.sin(a)]);
      }
      for(let i=0;i<14;i++){
        const a = 2*Math.PI*i/14 + 0.05*(rng()-0.5);
        pts.push([ 1.1 + 0.6*Math.cos(a), 0.6*Math.sin(a)]);
      }
    } else {
      for(let i=0;i<24;i++){ pts.push([2*rng()-1, 2*rng()-1]); }
    }
    return pts;
  }
  let pts = buildPoints(datasets[0]);
  function pairDist(a,b){ const dx=a[0]-b[0], dy=a[1]-b[1]; return Math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy); }
  function uniteFind(parent,x){ while(parent[x]!==x){ parent[x]=parent[parent[x]]; x=parent[x]; } return x; }
  function bettiCounts(n,edges,triangles){
    const parent = Array.from({length:n},(_,i)=>i);
    for(const [u,v] of edges){
      const ru=uniteFind(parent,u), rv=uniteFind(parent,v);
      if(ru!==rv) parent[ru]=rv;
    }
    const roots = new Set();
    for(let i=0;i<n;i++) roots.add(uniteFind(parent,i));
    const beta0 = roots.size;
    const chi = n - edges.length + triangles.length;
    // β₁ = β₀ − χ + β₂. For Vietoris–Rips on R² point clouds, β₂ = 0 in
    // practice (no 2-sphere can be triangulated by 2D vertices), so we drop
    // the β₂ term — but clamp to ≥ 0 to surface any future violation rather
    // than show a negative count.
    const beta1 = Math.max(0, beta0 - chi);
    return [beta0, beta1];
  }
  function render(){
    while(svg.firstChild) svg.removeChild(svg.firstChild);
    const eps = (+sl.value)/100;
    ev.textContent = eps.toFixed(2);
    const W=720, H=320, midL=180, midR=540, midY=160, scale=120;
    function px(p, cx){ return [cx + p[0]*scale, midY + p[1]*scale]; }
    const edges=[];
    for(let i=0;i<pts.length;i++) for(let j=i+1;j<pts.length;j++){
      if(pairDist(pts[i],pts[j]) <= 2*eps) edges.push([i,j]);
    }
    const adj = Array.from({length:pts.length},()=>new Set());
    for(const [u,v] of edges){ adj[u].add(v); adj[v].add(u); }
    const triangles=[];
    for(let i=0;i<pts.length;i++) for(let j=i+1;j<pts.length;j++){
      if(!adj[i].has(j)) continue;
      for(const k of adj[i]){
        if(k>j && adj[j].has(k)) triangles.push([i,j,k]);
      }
    }
    svg.appendChild(SVG('text',{x:midL, y:24, 'text-anchor':'middle','font-size':12, fill:'var(--mute)'})).textContent = 'point cloud + balls';
    for(const p of pts){
      const [x,y] = px(p, midL);
      svg.appendChild(SVG('circle',{cx:x, cy:y, r:eps*scale, fill:'var(--cyan)', 'fill-opacity':0.10, stroke:'var(--cyan)', 'stroke-opacity':0.35, 'stroke-width':0.8}));
    }
    svg.appendChild(SVG('text',{x:midR, y:24, 'text-anchor':'middle','font-size':12, fill:'var(--mute)'})).textContent = 'Vietoris–Rips complex';
    for(const [i,j,k] of triangles){
      const [x1,y1]=px(pts[i],midR), [x2,y2]=px(pts[j],midR), [x3,y3]=px(pts[k],midR);
      svg.appendChild(SVG('polygon',{points:`${x1},${y1} ${x2},${y2} ${x3},${y3}`, fill:'var(--yellow)','fill-opacity':0.18, stroke:'none'}));
    }
    for(const [u,v] of edges){
      const [x1,y1]=px(pts[u],midL), [x2,y2]=px(pts[v],midL);
      svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1,y1,x2,y2, stroke:'var(--blue)', 'stroke-width':1.2, 'stroke-opacity':0.55}));
      const [x3,y3]=px(pts[u],midR), [x4,y4]=px(pts[v],midR);
      svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:x3,y1:y3,x2:x4,y2:y4, stroke:'var(--blue)', 'stroke-width':1.2}));
    }
    for(const p of pts){
      const [xL,yL]=px(p,midL), [xR,yR]=px(p,midR);
      svg.appendChild(SVG('circle',{cx:xL,cy:yL,r:3, fill:'var(--ink)'}));
      svg.appendChild(SVG('circle',{cx:xR,cy:yR,r:3, fill:'var(--ink)'}));
    }
    const [b0,b1] = bettiCounts(pts.length, edges, triangles);
    out.textContent =
      `dataset: ${datasets[dataset]}   ε = ${eps.toFixed(2)}\n` +
      `|V| = ${pts.length}   |E| = ${edges.length}   |T| = ${triangles.length}\n` +
      `β₀ = ${b0}   β₁ = ${b1}     (β₀ = components, β₁ = independent loops)`;
  }
  sl.addEventListener('input', render);
  btn.addEventListener('click', ()=>{
    dataset = (dataset + 1) % datasets.length;
    pts = buildPoints(datasets[dataset]);
    render();
  });
  render();
})();
</script>

Persistent homology, the centerpiece of TDA, asks: as we sweep $\epsilon$ from $0$ to $\infty$, what topological features (components, loops, voids) persist over wide ranges of $\epsilon$, and which flicker briefly before dying?

2. Simplicial homology — the bookkeeping

Persistence runs simplicial homology in parallel at every scale, so we need the basics. Fix a field $k$ (typically $k=\mathbb{F}_2$ in software). For each abstract simplicial complex $K$, let $C_n(K)$ be the $k$-vector space with basis the $n$-simplices. The boundary $\partial_n : C_n \to C_{n-1}$ sends an oriented simplex to the alternating sum of its codimension-$1$ faces:

$\partial_n[v_0,\dots,v_n] \;=\; \sum_{i=0}^{n} (-1)^i \, [v_0,\dots,\widehat{v_i},\dots,v_n].$

The composite $\partial_{n-1} \circ \partial_n = 0$, so the kernel and image nest: $\mathrm{im}\,\partial_{n+1} \subseteq \ker\partial_n \subseteq C_n$. The $n$-th homology is the quotient

$H_n(K; k) \;=\; \ker \partial_n / \mathrm{im}\, \partial_{n+1}.$

Cycles modulo boundaries. The dimension $\beta_n = \dim_k H_n$ is the $n$-th Betti number: $\beta_0$ counts connected components, $\beta_1$ counts independent $1$-dim holes, $\beta_2$ counts enclosed voids. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$ the orientation signs vanish and the computation is row-reduction over $\mathbb{F}_2$ — fast, parallelisable, exactly what software wants.

    const beta1Note = filled ? 'β₁ = 0  (filled triangle is contractible)' : 'β₁ = 1  (empty triangle has one loop)';
    out.textContent =
      `chain c = ${chainName}\n` +
      `∂c = ${dName}\n` +
      `cycle? ${isCycle ? 'yes' : 'no'}     boundary? ${isBoundary ? 'yes (∂[ABC] = AB+BC+CA)' : 'no'}\n` +

3. Persistent homology — birth, death, barcode

Fix a filtration $\emptyset = K_0 \subseteq K_1 \subseteq \cdots \subseteq K_n = K$. Applying $H_k(-; k)$ to every inclusion gives a sequence of vector spaces and linear maps:

$H_k(K_0) \;\xrightarrow{f_0}\; H_k(K_1) \;\xrightarrow{f_1}\; \cdots \;\xrightarrow{f_{n-1}}\; H_k(K_n).$

This is a persistence module: a sequence of vector spaces tied together by maps. The data we want from it: when does a homology class first appear, and when does it become trivial?

For each pair $i \le j$, define the persistent homology group

$H_k^{i,j} \;=\; \mathrm{im}\bigl( H_k(K_i) \to H_k(K_j) \bigr),$

the classes in $K_j$ already present back at scale $i$. A class is born at $i$ if it lies in $H_k(K_i)$ but not in the image from $H_k(K_{i-1})$; it dies entering $K_j$ if it maps to zero in $H_k(K_j)$ but is non-zero in $H_k(K_{j-1})$.

Pack the bookkeeping into the persistence diagram (Cohen-Steiner–Edelsbrunner–Harer 2007): a multiset of points $(b,d) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ with $b < d$, one per born-then-killed class, plus the diagonal $\{(t,t)\}$ counted with infinite multiplicity. Equivalently, the barcode: one horizontal bar from $b$ to $d$ per feature. Long bars = robust features (e.g. a genuine loop in the data); short bars near the diagonal = topological noise.

<script>
(function(){
  const nSl=$('#tda-n'), nV=$('#tda-n-v'), noiseSl=$('#tda-noise'), noiseV=$('#tda-noise-v');
  const svg=$('#tda-bc-svg'), out=$('#tda-bc-out');
  function tdaRng(seed){
    let s = seed|0;
    return function(){
      s = (s + 0x6D2B79F5)|0;
      let t = Math.imul(s ^ s>>>15, s | 1);
      t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ t>>>7, t | 61);
      return ((t ^ t>>>14) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
    };
  }
  function sampleCircle(n, noise){
    const rng = tdaRng(20260513);
    const pts=[];
    for(let i=0;i<n;i++){
      const a = 2*Math.PI*i/n;
      const r = 1 + noise*(rng()-0.5);
      pts.push([r*Math.cos(a), r*Math.sin(a)]);
    }
    return pts;
  }
  function pairDist(a,b){ const dx=a[0]-b[0], dy=a[1]-b[1]; return Math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy); }
  function persistence(pts){
    const n = pts.length;
    const edges=[];
    for(let i=0;i<n;i++) for(let j=i+1;j<n;j++){
      edges.push([pairDist(pts[i],pts[j])/2, i, j]);
    }
    edges.sort((a,b)=>a[0]-b[0]);
    const tris=[];
    for(let i=0;i<n;i++) for(let j=i+1;j<n;j++) for(let k=j+1;k<n;k++){
      const t = Math.max(pairDist(pts[i],pts[j]), pairDist(pts[j],pts[k]), pairDist(pts[i],pts[k]))/2;
      tris.push([t,i,j,k]);
    }
    tris.sort((a,b)=>a[0]-b[0]);
    const parent = Array.from({length:n},(_,i)=>i);
    function find(x){ while(parent[x]!==x){ parent[x]=parent[parent[x]]; x=parent[x]; } return x; }
    const bars0 = [];
    let cycleBars = [];
    function ekey(i,j){ return i<j ? `${i}-${j}` : `${j}-${i}`; }
    let ti = 0;
    for(const [eps,i,j] of edges){
      const ri = find(i), rj = find(j);
      if(ri !== rj){
        bars0.push([0, eps]);
        parent[ri] = rj;
      } else {
        cycleBars.push({birth: eps, edges: new Set([ekey(i,j)])});
      }
      while(ti < tris.length && tris[ti][0] <= eps){
        const [tt,a,b,c] = tris[ti];
        const bd = new Set([ekey(a,b), ekey(b,c), ekey(a,c)]);
        cycleBars.sort((x,y)=>y.birth - x.birth);
        for(const cyc of cycleBars){
          if(cyc.death !== undefined) continue;
          let inter = 0;
          for(const ek of cyc.edges) if(bd.has(ek)) inter++;
          if(inter % 2 === 1){
            cyc.death = tt;
            break;
          }
        }
        ti++;
      }
    }
    const bars1 = [];
    for(const c of cycleBars){
      if(c.death === undefined) bars1.push([c.birth, Infinity]);
      else bars1.push([c.birth, c.death]);
    }
    bars0.push([0, Infinity]);
    return {bars0, bars1};
  }
  function render(){
    while(svg.firstChild) svg.removeChild(svg.firstChild);
    const n = +nSl.value; nV.textContent = n;
    const noise = (+noiseSl.value)/100; noiseV.textContent = noise.toFixed(2);
    const pts = sampleCircle(n, noise);
    const ML=170, midY=170, scale=110;
    svg.appendChild(SVG('text',{x:ML, y:24, 'text-anchor':'middle','font-size':12, fill:'var(--mute)'})).textContent = `${n} points on noisy circle`;
    for(const p of pts){
      svg.appendChild(SVG('circle',{cx:ML + p[0]*scale, cy:midY + p[1]*scale, r:3, fill:'var(--ink)'}));
    }
    const {bars0, bars1} = persistence(pts);
    const finiteVals = [...bars0.map(b=>b[1]).filter(Number.isFinite), ...bars1.map(b=>b[1]).filter(Number.isFinite)];
    const xmax = Math.max(0.5, ...finiteVals) * 1.10;
    const PX0=380, PX1=700, PY0=50, PYrow=12, infMark=PX1-10;
    function toX(t){ return PX0 + (Math.min(t, xmax)/xmax) * (PX1 - PX0); }
    svg.appendChild(SVG('text',{x:(PX0+PX1)/2, y:24, 'text-anchor':'middle','font-size':12, fill:'var(--mute)'})).textContent = 'persistence barcode';
    svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:PX0,y1:PY0-2,x2:PX1,y2:PY0-2, stroke:'var(--line)','stroke-width':1}));
    for(let t=0;t<=xmax;t += Math.max(0.1, xmax/5)){
      const x = toX(t);
      svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:x,y1:PY0-4,x2:x,y2:PY0, stroke:'var(--mute)'}));
      svg.appendChild(SVG('text',{x, y:PY0-8, 'text-anchor':'middle','font-size':10, fill:'var(--mute)'})).textContent = t.toFixed(1);
    }
    const sorted0 = bars0.slice().sort((a,b)=>(Number.isFinite(b[1])?b[1]:1e9)-(Number.isFinite(a[1])?a[1]:1e9));
    let row=0;
    for(const [b,d] of sorted0){
      const x1 = toX(b);
      const x2 = Number.isFinite(d) ? toX(d) : infMark;
      const y = PY0 + 12 + row*PYrow;
      svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1,x2,y1:y,y2:y, stroke:'var(--cyan)', 'stroke-width':3, 'stroke-linecap':'round'}));
      if(!Number.isFinite(d)) svg.appendChild(SVG('text',{x:infMark+5, y:y+3, 'font-size':10, fill:'var(--cyan)'})).textContent = '∞';
      row++;
      if(row >= 12 && sorted0.length > 12){ const y = PY0 + 12 + row*PYrow; svg.appendChild(SVG('text',{x:PX0, y:y+3, 'font-size':10, fill:'var(--mute)','font-style':'italic'})).textContent = `+${sorted0.length-12} more β₀ bars (longest shown above)`; break; } if(row > 12) break;
    }
    svg.appendChild(SVG('text',{x:PX0, y:PY0 + 24 + Math.min(12,sorted0.length)*PYrow + (sorted0.length>12?PYrow:0), 'font-size':11, fill:'var(--yellow)'})).textContent = 'β₁ bars:';
    let row1 = Math.min(12,sorted0.length) + 1;
    const sorted1 = bars1.slice().sort((a,b)=>{
      const dA = Number.isFinite(a[1]) ? a[1]-a[0] : 1e9;
      const dB = Number.isFinite(b[1]) ? b[1]-b[0] : 1e9;
      return dB - dA;
    });
    let longestBar1 = null;
    for(const [b,d] of sorted1){
      const x1 = toX(b);
      const x2 = Number.isFinite(d) ? toX(d) : infMark;
      const y = PY0 + 12 + row1*PYrow;
      const lenCur = Number.isFinite(d) ? d-b : Infinity;
      const lenBest = longestBar1 ? (Number.isFinite(longestBar1.d) ? longestBar1.d-longestBar1.b : Infinity) : -1;
      if(lenCur > lenBest) longestBar1 = {b, d};
      svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1,x2,y1:y,y2:y, stroke:'var(--yellow)', 'stroke-width':3, 'stroke-linecap':'round'}));
      if(!Number.isFinite(d)) svg.appendChild(SVG('text',{x:infMark+5, y:y+3, 'font-size':10, fill:'var(--yellow)'})).textContent = '∞';
      row1++;
      if(row1 >= 22 && sorted1.length > (22 - Math.min(12,sorted0.length) - 1)){ const y = PY0 + 12 + row1*PYrow; svg.appendChild(SVG('text',{x:PX0, y:y+3, 'font-size':10, fill:'var(--mute)','font-style':'italic'})).textContent = `(more β₁ bars truncated — see β₁-count in readout)`; break; } if(row1 > 22) break;
    }
    const longest = longestBar1 ? `[${longestBar1.b.toFixed(2)}, ${Number.isFinite(longestBar1.d)?longestBar1.d.toFixed(2):'∞'}]` : 'none';
    out.textContent =
      `n = ${n} points,  noise = ${noise.toFixed(2)}\n` +
      `β₀ bars: ${bars0.length} (one persists to ∞ — the whole cloud is eventually connected)\n` +
      `β₁ bars: ${bars1.length}   longest: ${longest}\n` +
      `Reading: long β₁ bar = robust loop signature; bars near the diagonal = topological noise.`;
  }
  nSl.addEventListener('input', render);
  noiseSl.addEventListener('input', render);
  render();
})();
</script>

blocks.html: The map $X \mapsto \mathrm{Dgm}_k(X)$ from input filtration to persistence diagram is the central pipeline of TDA. The next two sections explain why it is well-behaved: it is stable under input perturbation (§4) and uniquely encoded as a barcode (§5).

4. Stability — small input perturbations cause small diagram perturbations

For TDA to be useful on real data, the persistence diagram must be robust to noise. The stability theorem of Cohen-Steiner, Edelsbrunner, and Harer (2007) supplies exactly that guarantee.

Compare two filtrations by tame functions $f, g : K \to \mathbb{R}$ on the same complex (think: distance to two nearby point clouds). Define the bottleneck distance between their persistence diagrams as

$W_\infty\bigl(\mathrm{Dgm}(f), \mathrm{Dgm}(g)\bigr) \;=\; \inf_{\gamma} \;\sup_{p} \; \|p - \gamma(p)\|_\infty,$

where $\gamma$ ranges over partial matchings between the two diagrams (with unmatched points sent to their nearest diagonal point). Then:

Stability theorem. $W_\infty\bigl(\mathrm{Dgm}(f), \mathrm{Dgm}(g)\bigr) \;\le\; \|f - g\|_\infty$.

Persistence is $1$-Lipschitz with respect to the $L^\infty$ norm on input filtrations. For point-cloud Rips filtrations, the same statement reads: the Hausdorff distance between two clouds bounds the bottleneck distance between their persistence diagrams. Noisy data $\Rightarrow$ noisy diagrams, but only as noisy as the data.

blocks.html: Two practical consequences: (i) Hausdorff-close point clouds yield bottleneck-close diagrams, so persistence-based features are statistical; (ii) noise floor estimation: bars with $d - b$ smaller than the input noise can be discarded.
</section>

5. Structure theorem — barcodes are the complete invariant

What does a persistence module look like as an algebraic object? The classification is clean.

For each interval $[b, d) \subset \mathbb{R}$ (allowing $d = +\infty$), the interval module $\mathbb{I}[b,d)$ is the persistence module that assigns $k$ to every $t \in [b,d)$ and $0$ elsewhere, with all transition maps either the identity or zero. Pictorially, $\mathbb{I}[b,d)$ is a single bar from $b$ to $d$.

Structure theorem (Crawley-Boevey, Zomorodian–Carlsson). Every pointwise-finite-dimensional persistence module $M$ over a field decomposes uniquely (up to reordering) as a direct sum of interval modules: $$M \;\cong\; \bigoplus_{\alpha} \mathbb{I}[b_\alpha, d_\alpha).$$ The multiset $\{(b_\alpha, d_\alpha)\}$ is the persistence diagram of $M$.

The persistence diagram is therefore a complete invariant: two pointwise-finite persistence modules are isomorphic iff their diagrams are equal as multisets. No hidden algebraic data beyond the bars.

The proof goes via the category of finitely-presented graded modules over $k[t]$ — the same machinery as the structure theorem for finitely generated modules over a PID. The algebraic punchline is that $k[t]$ is a PID, and the indecomposable summands of a finitely generated graded $k[t]$-module are exactly the interval modules.

The multi-parameter generalization is genuinely harder: a persistence module indexed by $\mathbb{R}^2$ (e.g. density + scale) does not decompose into rectangles — there is no analogous structure theorem in two or more parameters. This is the active multi-parameter persistence frontier.

6. Mapper — a skeleton of the data

Persistent homology summarizes a point cloud as a multiset of bars. Mapper (Singh, Mémoli & Carlsson, 2007) summarizes it as a graph — a 1-dimensional skeleton showing the cloud's branching structure.

The algorithm:

  1. Choose a filter function $f : X \to \mathbb{R}^k$ (e.g. $L^2$-norm, density estimate, first PCA coordinate, a learned embedding coordinate).
  2. Cover $f(X)$ by overlapping intervals (or hypercubes) $U_1,\dots,U_m$ with overlap fraction $p$.
  3. For each $U_i$, run a clustering algorithm (single-linkage, DBSCAN) on $f^{-1}(U_i) \cap X$. Each cluster is a Mapper node.
  4. Two nodes are connected by an edge iff they share a point in $X$ — i.e. their underlying clusters intersect. (Higher simplices for triple intersections, etc., make it a full simplicial complex; in practice the graph suffices.)

The output is the nerve of the cover by clusters. The flexibility to pick $f$ and the cover is both a strength (it can be tuned to the question) and a hazard (it must be tuned responsibly).

  }
  function buildY(){
    const r = rng(424242);
    const pts=[];
    function arm(theta, n){
      for(let i=0;i<n;i++){
        const t = 0.05 + 0.95*i/(n-1);
        const x = t*Math.cos(theta) + 0.04*(r()-0.5);
        const y = t*Math.sin(theta) + 0.04*(r()-0.5);
        pts.push([x,y]);
      }
    }
    arm(0, 14);
    arm(2.4, 14);
    arm(-2.4, 14);
    return pts;

  const pts = buildY();
  function clusterByDistance(indices, all, eps){
    const parent = {};
    for(const idx of indices) parent[idx] = idx;
    function find(i){ while(parent[i]!==i){ parent[i] = parent[parent[i]]; i = parent[i]; } return i; }
    for(let i=0;i<indices.length;i++) for(let j=i+1;j<indices.length;j++){
      const a = all[indices[i]], b = all[indices[j]];
      const d = Math.hypot(a[0]-b[0], a[1]-b[1]);
      if(d <= eps){
        const ri = find(indices[i]), rj = find(indices[j]);
        if(ri!==rj) parent[ri] = rj;
      }
    }
    const groups = new Map();
    for(const idx of indices){
      const root = find(idx);
      if(!groups.has(root)) groups.set(root, []);
      groups.get(root).push(idx);
    }
    return [...groups.values()];
  }

    while(svg.firstChild) svg.removeChild(svg.firstChild);
    const nBins = +bSl.value; bV.textContent = nBins;
    const overlap = (+oSl.value)/100; oV.textContent = overlap.toFixed(2);
    const xs = pts.map(p=>p[0]);
    const xmin = Math.min(...xs), xmax = Math.max(...xs);
    const span = xmax - xmin;
    const binW = span/nBins;
    const slack = binW * overlap;
    const bins = [];
    for(let i=0;i<nBins;i++){
      const lo = xmin + i*binW - slack;
      const hi = xmin + (i+1)*binW + slack;
      const inside = [];
      for(let j=0;j<pts.length;j++){ if(pts[j][0] >= lo && pts[j][0] <= hi) inside.push(j); }
      bins.push({lo,hi,inside});
    }
    const clusters = [];
    for(let b=0;b<bins.length;b++){
      const gs = clusterByDistance(bins[b].inside, pts, 0.22);
      for(const g of gs){
        let xc=0,yc=0;
        for(const idx of g){ xc += pts[idx][0]; yc += pts[idx][1]; }
        xc/=g.length; yc/=g.length;
        clusters.push({bin:b, members:new Set(g), xc, yc, size:g.length});
      }
    }
    const edges = [];
    for(let i=0;i<clusters.length;i++) for(let j=i+1;j<clusters.length;j++){
      let share = 0;
      for(const m of clusters[i].members){ if(clusters[j].members.has(m)) { share++; break; } }
      if(share) edges.push([i,j]);
    }
    const ML=180, midY=180, scale=120;
    svg.appendChild(SVG('text',{x:ML, y:24, 'text-anchor':'middle','font-size':12, fill:'var(--mute)'})).textContent = `Y cloud + bins (filter = x)`;
    for(let b=0;b<bins.length;b++){
      const x1 = ML + bins[b].lo*scale;
      const x2 = ML + bins[b].hi*scale;
      const fill = b%2===0 ? 'var(--cyan)' : 'var(--yellow)';
      svg.appendChild(SVG('rect',{x:x1, y:80, width:x2-x1, height:200, fill, 'fill-opacity':0.07, stroke:'none'}));
    }
    for(const p of pts){
      svg.appendChild(SVG('circle',{cx:ML + p[0]*scale, cy:midY + p[1]*scale, r:2.5, fill:'var(--ink)'}));
    }
    const PX=480, PY=180, R=120;
    svg.appendChild(SVG('text',{x:PX+R/2, y:24, 'text-anchor':'middle','font-size':12, fill:'var(--mute)'})).textContent = `nerve graph (${clusters.length} nodes, ${edges.length} edges)`;
    for(const [i,j] of edges){
      const a = clusters[i], b = clusters[j];
      const x1 = PX + (a.bin + 0.5)/nBins * R*1.5;
      const y1 = PY + a.yc*70;
      const x2 = PX + (b.bin + 0.5)/nBins * R*1.5;
      const y2 = PY + b.yc*70;
      svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1,y1,x2,y2, stroke:'var(--mute)','stroke-width':1.5}));
    }
    for(const c of clusters){
      const x = PX + (c.bin + 0.5)/nBins * R*1.5;
      const y = PY + c.yc*70;
      const r = 4 + 1.8*Math.sqrt(c.size);
      svg.appendChild(SVG('circle',{cx:x, cy:y, r, fill:'var(--violet)', stroke:'var(--ink)','stroke-width':1}));
    }
    const deg = new Map();
    for(const [i,j] of edges){ deg.set(i,(deg.get(i)||0)+1); deg.set(j,(deg.get(j)||0)+1); }
    let branches = 0;
    for(const d of deg.values()) if(d>=3) branches++;
    out.textContent =
      `bins = ${nBins}   overlap = ${overlap.toFixed(2)}\n` +
      `clusters = ${clusters.length}   edges = ${edges.length}   degree-≥3 nodes = ${branches}\n` +
      `Reading: a degree-3 node = Mapper recovered the Y's branch point. Tune the cover until it appears stably.`;
  }
  bSl.addEventListener('input', render);
  oSl.addEventListener('input', render);
  render();
})();
</script>

blocks.html: Mapper is the workhorse of "exploratory TDA" outside academia: the original paper visualised diabetes patient strata with it; Carlsson's company Ayasdi (founded 2008, acquired by SymphonyAI 2019) built a commercial platform around it. Caveats: Mapper graphs are not a topological invariant — they depend on $f$ and the cover — so they are best read as hypothesis generators, then validated with persistent homology or domain knowledge.
</section>

7. Cohomology, Reeb graphs, and the broader toolkit

Persistence has spawned a family of related constructions; the four worth knowing:

Persistent cohomology

By duality $H^k(K_i) = H_k(K_i)^*$ when $K_i$ is finite, so the cohomological bars equal the homological bars (over a field). What's gained operationally: cohomology yields cocycles, and certain cocycles (1-cocycles with $\mathbb{S}^1$ coefficients, after lifting) can be used as circular coordinates — explicit angle-valued maps $X \to S^1$ encoding loops in the data. Persistent cohomology is also strictly faster in practice than persistent homology (de Silva–Morozov–Vejdemo-Johansson 2011): the "cohomology shortcut" inverts the matrix once instead of computing column reductions.

Zigzag persistence

Standard persistence requires a single filtration direction. Zigzag persistence (Carlsson–de Silva 2010) allows the direction to switch: $K_0 \to K_1 \leftarrow K_2 \to K_3 \leftarrow \cdots$ models filtrations with merges, sliding windows of time-varying point clouds, or two different filtrations to compare. The Gabriel-quiver classification of $A_n$-type representations still gives a barcode.

Multi-parameter persistence

A two-parameter persistence module $\{V_{s,t}\}$ indexed by $(s,t) \in \mathbb{R}^2$ does not decompose into rectangle-shaped indecomposables: the moduli of indecomposables is wild. Surrogate invariants (rank invariant, fibered barcode, persistence landscape, $\Lambda$-Hilbert function, GRIL) are the field's active research direction.

Reeb graphs & mergetrees

The Reeb graph of $(X, f : X \to \mathbb{R})$ identifies points of $X$ whose preimages lie in the same connected component of $f^{-1}(t)$ — a 1-D skeleton encoding the level-set topology. Mapper is a discrete approximation. Merge trees are the $\beta_0$-only sub-summary, used in scalar-field visualization since the 1990s.

Software ecosystem

  • Ripser (Bauer 2019) — fastest Rips persistence; the de facto standard for moderate-scale clouds.
  • GUDHI (INRIA) — broad C++/Python library: Rips, Čech, Alpha complexes, Mapper, multi-parameter, Wasserstein metrics.
  • Dionysus (Morozov) — research-oriented, supports zigzag and cohomology.
  • scikit-tda — Python umbrella (Ripser, Mapper-via-KeplerMapper, persim).
  • giotto-tda — sklearn-style API; emphasises ML pipelines.

<script>
(function(){
  const code=$('#tda-ripser-code'), runBtn=$('#tda-ripser-run'), outPre=$('#tda-ripser-out'), warn=$('#tda-ripser-warn');
  const prelude = `
function ripsPersistence(pts){
  function pairDist(a,b){ const dx=a[0]-b[0], dy=a[1]-b[1]; return Math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy); }
  const n=pts.length;
  const edges=[];
  for(let i=0;i<n;i++) for(let j=i+1;j<n;j++) edges.push([pairDist(pts[i],pts[j])/2,i,j]);
  edges.sort((a,b)=>a[0]-b[0]);
  const tris=[];
  for(let i=0;i<n;i++) for(let j=i+1;j<n;j++) for(let k=j+1;k<n;k++){
    const t = Math.max(pairDist(pts[i],pts[j]), pairDist(pts[j],pts[k]), pairDist(pts[i],pts[k]))/2;
    tris.push([t,i,j,k]);
  }
  tris.sort((a,b)=>a[0]-b[0]);
  const parent=Array.from({length:n},(_,i)=>i);
  function find(x){ while(parent[x]!==x){ parent[x]=parent[parent[x]]; x=parent[x]; } return x; }
  function ek(i,j){ return i<j ? i+'-'+j : j+'-'+i; }
  const bars0=[]; const cycles=[];
  let ti=0;
  for(const [eps,i,j] of edges){
    const ri=find(i), rj=find(j);
    if(ri!==rj){ bars0.push([0,eps]); parent[ri]=rj; }
    else { cycles.push({birth:eps, edges:new Set([ek(i,j)]), death:undefined}); }
    while(ti<tris.length && tris[ti][0]<=eps){
      const [tt,a,b,c]=tris[ti];
      const bd=new Set([ek(a,b),ek(b,c),ek(a,c)]);
      cycles.sort((x,y)=>y.birth-x.birth);
      for(const cy of cycles){
        if(cy.death!==undefined) continue;
        let inter=0; for(const k of cy.edges) if(bd.has(k)) inter++;
        if(inter%2===1){ cy.death=tt; break; }
      }
      ti++;
    }
  }
  bars0.push([0,Infinity]);
  const bars1 = cycles.map(c=>[c.birth, c.death===undefined?Infinity:c.death]);
  return {bars0, bars1};
}
`;
  function runSandboxed(source){
    const log = [];
    const sandbox = { console: { log: (...args)=>log.push(args.map(a=>JSON.stringify(a)).join(' ')) } };
    try {
      const fn = new Function('console', 'Math', 'JSON', prelude + '\n' + source);
      fn(sandbox.console, Math, JSON);
      return { ok:true, log };
    } catch(err){
      return { ok:false, error: err.message, log };
    }
  }
  runBtn.addEventListener('click', ()=>{
    warn.textContent = 'running…';
    const res = runSandboxed(code.value);
    if(res.ok){
      warn.textContent = 'ran successfully · ' + new Date().toLocaleTimeString();
      outPre.textContent = res.log.join('\n');
    } else {
      warn.textContent = 'error';
      outPre.textContent = (res.log.length ? res.log.join('\n') + '\n' : '') + 'Error: ' + res.error;
    }
  });
  runBtn.click();
})();
</script>

8. Connections

TDA sits at the meeting of algebraic topology, combinatorics, statistics, and applied computation. The frontier is plural: multi-parameter persistence (no structure theorem), differentiable persistence (gradient-based learning over diagrams), and "topology-aware deep learning" (persistence loss layers, persistence-stabilised features). The unsettled question is whether persistence buys real predictive lift on noisy real-world data or merely a sophisticated descriptor; the empirical jury is split.

  • Algebraic topology — singular homology — the textbook companion to the simplicial homology used pointwise here; the long exact sequence of a pair sits behind every persistence calculation.
  • Simplicial complexes — combinatorial persistence — sister page focused on the combinatorial $f$-vectors and Stanley–Reisner machinery underneath the Rips and Čech constructions.
  • Spectral methods for massive data sets — graph Laplacian — the linear-algebraic complement to TDA on data; the Laplacian eigenvectors recover $\beta_0$ as the multiplicity of 0, but say nothing about higher-dimensional features.
  • High-dimensional geometry — concentration of measure — concentration phenomena explain why Mapper covers and Rips scales work at all: in high dimensions, typical pairwise distances cluster tightly, sharpening the persistence diagram's signal.
  • Homological algebra — chain complexes & exact sequences — the algebraic backbone: every persistence computation is a chain-complex computation with the filtration imposed as a grading.
